newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee exports may exceed ACPC limit -trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee exports may exceed ACPC limit -trade.

text.p: Brazil January-June coffee exports are likely to exceed the six million 60-kg bags agreed by members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) but this should not cause any concern, traders said.
"Exports should pass the limit but not by a great deal, I think 10 percent more would be acceptable," said Jair Coser, president of leading coffee exporter Unicafe.
Brazil has already shipped 3.89 million bags in the first quarter of this year and export registrations for the second three months reached 3.20 million bags by April 25.
Trade estimates for actual April shipments generally converge around 1.2 to 1.3 million bags, with bills of lading covering 1.19 million bags by May 2.
Opinions differ however over possible May exports, with some traders anticipating less than one million bags and others higher shipments than in April of up to one million bags.
As of April 25, export registrations for May were 1.39 million bags.

The outlook for June is for very low exports indeed, not necessarily because of a lack of supply but because roasters are likely to hold out for the lower prices of July/August shipment coffees, dealers said.
"My guess is that in June roasters are only going to buy what they really need to," one trader said.
This view is confirmed by the low export registrations of only 339,000 bags for June shipment.
Brazil therefore could end up shipping between 6.5 million and over seven million bags in the January to June period.
Traders do not anticipate however the Brazilian government, battling to plug its widening trade gap, would take any measures which would impact negatively on export revenue.
Instead they expect a May 21 ACPC council session in London to discuss allowing Brazil to anticipate any quotas which may be applied for July to December 1997.
"For the government, the trade balance is much more important. I think they will simply go to the ACPC and talk about it there," one dealer said.
